interpretation: Allocator/GC and host canonical/lifetime setup are the largest coarse LLGo profile group, not an exact exclusive CPU decomposition. Compiler upgrade resolves lower allocation counts, not normalGC CPU gain. Final fresh Caller batching and immutable metadata lower allocations/bytes and instructions; CPU/throughput gains remain unproven. Reject host-state coallocation:408byte allocation crosses BDWGC tiny-list routing, unlike152+256byte base. Source ablation reproduces its adverse noGC point, exact layout/allocator cost shares unisolated. Getg outlines reduce instructions without CPU gain and are rejected. No competitive parity/release acceptance.
errata: Original getg-no-gc-16 template removed GC_DONT_GC, stopped on nonzero collections before any row serialization; four process executions from that failed block are not recovered/countable. Independent corrected cohorts retained separately.

Initial host-metadata Go build used phase instead of P3 runner; wrong-flag preflight and failed startup block serialized no valid rows. Corrected independent Go cohorts are separate; no result inferred from failed startup.
Initial coallocation plain branch used a nil multiassignment LHS; Go tests caught it before timing and it was corrected.
A new result-handoff test initially tried reuse after a trapping callback, contrary to the instance failure contract; corrected test puts failure last.
Initial allocation-site diagnostic omitted the final flush and wrote no profile; corrected untimed run includes flush.
A first new Caller test referred to vm.ErrClosed rather than wasm.ErrClosed and failed to compile; fixed before timed work.

Go CPU Profiler produced one sample and is insufficient for a distribution claim. Time Profiler Running rows include kernel waits; CPU-cycle weights are not cross-runtime exclusive-cost units. Raw summaries and all adverse controls remain.
